newsitem.title: USA: Call to 911 discounted in Colorado girl's murder.
newsitem.headline: Call to 911 discounted in Colorado girl's murder.

text.p: Police investigating the murder of six-year-old beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey Friday said there was no link between the child's slaying and a phone call placed to police from the residence three days before her body was found.
"It appears that during a party at the home a telephone user misdialed while making a long-distance call," Boulder, Colorado police said in a statement.

Several news organisations reported the 911 telephone call had been made from the 15-room Tudor style home, but that whoever dialed immediately hung up. A Boulder police officer was dispatched to the home after the call and found out about the mistaken dialing, police said.
That was the only information released Friday on the murder, which has grabbed national attention.
Thursday night Boulder Police Chief Tom Koby held a news briefing which was telecast on a community cable channel in Boulder, but he offered little new information on the case.

The parents, John and Patricia Ramsey, remain secluded in a Boulder location and have yet to agree to be formally interviewed by the police. No arrests have been made and no suspects named in the Dec. 26 murder.
The little girl's body was found by her father in a windowless room in the basement of her home some eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note on a staircase, demanding $118,000.
She was strangled. Koby declined to comment on published reports said she had also been sexually assaulted.
